content:
With the starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max being US$100 higher than the previous generation, Apple has also applied price increases across the entire iPhone lineup, including some models whose specifications remain completely unchanged.

In other words, the base iPhone 17 has risen from US$799 to US$899; the iPhone Air has officially crossed the four-digit threshold, with a starting price of US$1,099.

The iPhone 17e and iPhone 16 have also seen increases of US$100. The iPhone 17e has risen from its previous base price of US$599 to US$699.

Of course, what consumers may find frustrating is that some iPhone models have been on sale for a year with no changes to their specifications, yet their prices have actually gone up.

However, Apple continues to adjust according to market changes to cope with rising costs of components such as RAM and storage chips, and the increase is 'only' US$100 — actually lower than what some analysts had originally expected.

Below is the complete iPhone pricing list after this round of price increases:

  • iPhone 17e: 256GB for US$699
  • iPhone 16: 128GB for US$799
  • iPhone 17: 256GB for US$899
  • iPhone Air: 256GB for US$1,099
  • iPhone 18 Pro: 256GB for US$1,199
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: 256GB for US$1,299
  • iPhone Duo: 256GB for US$1,999

With the arrival of the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 17 Pro has been discontinued. The base iPhone 17 is expected to be replaced by a new iPhone in spring 2027.

Apple has adjusted its product launch schedule — this autumn will see only new high-end models released, while updates to the base and Air lineups are expected in March or April next year.
